claim_text: Nikola Tesla said: If you only knew the magnificence of the 3, 6 and 9, then you would have a key to the universe.
notes: Viral quotation; exact wording and earliest occurrence require archival search.

claim_text: Nikola Tesla said that the secrets of the universe should be understood through energy, frequency, and vibration.
notes: Frequently attributed wording; authenticate exact or materially equivalent primary passage.

claim_text: Nikola Tesla said that his brain was only a receiver and that the universe contained a core from which knowledge is obtained.
notes: Quotation candidate; investigate the earliest traceable wording.

claim_text: Nikola Tesla said: The present is theirs; the future, for which I really worked, is mine.
notes: Quotation candidate; punctuation and wording variants must remain in one canonical family.

claim_text: Nikola Tesla said that he did not care that others stole his idea but cared that they had no ideas of their own.
notes: Quotation candidate; search Tesla texts and later biography transmission.

claim_text: Nikola Tesla told someone that their hate could light the whole world if it were turned into electricity.
notes: Often framed as a personal reply; identify addressee and documentary origin.

claim_text: Nikola Tesla said that scientists of his day thought deeply instead of clearly.
notes: Quotation candidate; search interview and magazine archives.

claim_text: Nikola Tesla said that being alone was the secret of invention because ideas are born in solitude.
notes: Quotation candidate; distinguish paraphrase from exact quotation.

claim_text: Nikola Tesla wrote that all repeated acts or operations he performed had to be divisible by three.
notes: Primary-text lead exists in My Inventions; verify against a scan before authentication.

claim_text: Nikola Tesla always walked around a building three times before entering it.
notes: Popular biographical claim; determine whether primary or later biography evidence exists.

claim_text: Nikola Tesla would stay only in hotel rooms whose numbers were divisible by three.
notes: Popular biographical claim; search hotel records and early biographies.

claim_text: Nikola Tesla believed that the numbers 3, 6, and 9 formed a special cosmic code.
notes: Interpretive belief claim; divisible-by-three behavior cannot authenticate it by itself.

claim_text: Nikola Tesla developed and patented key elements of a practical polyphase alternating-current system.
notes: Search patents and contemporaneous engineering records; avoid broader inventor-of-AC wording.

claim_text: Nikola Tesla invented alternating current.
notes: Broad popular claim; separate AC history from Tesla's polyphase-system contributions.

claim_text: Nikola Tesla patented a method and apparatus for remotely controlling a moving vessel or vehicle in 1898.
notes: Patent US613809A is a primary lead; verify dates and claim wording.

claim_text: Nikola Tesla invented radio.
notes: Historically complex priority claim; avoid binary judgment without explicit criteria.

claim_text: The United States Supreme Court officially declared Nikola Tesla to be the inventor of radio.
notes: Check the 1943 judgment itself; distinguish patent-claim invalidation from an inventor declaration.

claim_text: Nikola Tesla invented X-rays before Wilhelm Röntgen.
notes: Priority claim; distinguish experimentation and imaging from discovery.

claim_text: Nikola Tesla invented radar decades before its recognized development.
notes: Priority claim; distinguish prediction, component ideas, and an operational radar system.

claim_text: Nikola Tesla predicted portable wireless devices capable of distant voice and image communication.
notes: 1926 interview lead exists; authenticate wording against the original magazine scan.
